content.text:
All the helpers are gone from `tests/Fixture` and every test that used them is now written out flat. My tests all pass except one unrelated failure: 1876 of 1877 pass in the requested run, and the pbt run of `GraphPropertyTest` passes too. The failure is `tests/Unit/Config/OutputFormatTest.php`, which I didn't touch. Someone's uncommitted change to `src/Config/OutputFormat.php` adds a `Mermaid` case but that test still expects the old list of formats. PHPStan reports no errors on every file I touched, and on `src/Analyzer`, `src/Config` and their tests, so the "every public method has a test" rule holds. php-cs-fixer is clean. I didn't run the full installed-package sweep; its guard test and one package (`composer/semver`) pass.

## Deleted
- `tests/Fixture/Analyzer/`: `ParsedSnippet.php`, `GraphSpelling.php`, `WrittenAutoloadMaps.php`, `InstalledPackages.php`, `FailingCollector.php`
- `tests/Fixture/Graph/StubNode.php` and `StubEdge.php`, `tests/Fixture/Config/StubConfigReader.php`, and the two emptied directories

## Rewritten
- **NativeAnalyzer unit tests (all 14 files):** each test parses its snippet inline with php-parser, or writes files into a vfsStream project (already a dev dependency) and reads them with `SourceIndex::of`. No temp directories. Expected values are literal `Node`/`Edge`/`SymbolDeclaration`/`TraitMethod` objects compared with `assertEquals`. I broke one expectation on purpose to confirm these comparisons do fail.
- **Walker tests** now call the method each test is named after (`walkClassLike`, `descend`, `member`, `method`, `traitUse`) instead of always going through `walkFile`.
- **`EquivalenceCorpus.php`** is now a single `public const SCENARIOS`; its data fingerprint is identical before and after, including after formatting. I kept it as source strings rather than a folder of `.php` files: php-cs-fixer formats every `*.php` in the repo, some scenarios depend on line layout, and the deliberately broken scenario would fail lint.
- **The two corpus contract tests** write the scenario files themselves. The coverage test is now one assertion per question: the sorted kinds found must equal every `NodeKind` (except `Builtin`) and every `EdgeKind`.
- **`InstalledPackageEquivalenceTest`:** package discovery moved into its data provider; it finds the same 36 packages as before.
- **`GraphPropertyTest`:** each drawn relation is an anonymous `Edge` written where it is added.
- **`AuthoredEdgeTest`:** uses a real `MethodCallEdge` instead of a stub.
- **`ConfigLoaderTest`:** the stub readers are anonymous `ConfigReader` classes.
- **`ConfigReaderTest`:** two tests only exercised the stub itself. I replaced them with real readers that know nothing (an empty environment prefix, a missing YAML file).
- **`ContainerFactoryTest`:** uses `InClassMethodCollector` instead of the failing collector.
- **`PhpStanAnalyzerTest`:** `FailingCollector` is declared at the bottom of this file in a second namespace, `Tests\Double`, as you chose (option c). Nothing else references it.

Only `#[Small]` tests are actually checked for missing `#[UsesClass]`. Mine are all complete, and I confirmed the check fires by removing one. Medium and Large tests are never checked, so I left them with just `#[CoversClass]`, as the files had before.

## Where the src interface made flat tests awkward
- **PhpStanAnalyzer takes collectors only as class names, so a failing collector must be a named class.** PHPStan builds collectors from names written into a config file, so an anonymous class or PHPUnit stub can't be used. The project's static-analysis rules also refuse a named helper class inside a `Tests\Unit` file, which is why it needed a second namespace.
- **Everything in NativeAnalyzer expects code whose names are already resolved**, but the type system can't say so, and the only producers of that input read files (`SourceIndex::parse` / `SourceIndex::of`). So every test either repeats the parse-and-resolve steps inline or writes a virtual file first.
- **The walkers need four things before any question can be asked:** an index, a recorder, a walker, and the file taken back out of the index.
- **`ClassWalker` and `SourceWalker` depend on each other through their constructors.** To test `ClassWalker` you must build a `SourceWalker`, which quietly builds a second `ClassWalker` of its own.
- **Each per-kind `UsageEmitter` method (e.g. `constantFetch`) takes four arguments**, including a source node and location that `emit()` normally works out itself. They seem to be public only because the project's rules forbid private methods and require a test for every public one.
- **`AnalysisScope::resolveFunctionName` depends on a hidden detail of the parse** (an attribute the name resolver attaches), not on anything in its signature.
- **`SourceIndex`'s public constructor expects maps with lower-cased keys**, so building one by hand means copying what `of()` does internally.
- **The engine types limit which nodes each edge can join**, so testing the graph's own bookkeeping across every edge kind needs an anonymous `Edge`.

## Src behaviour that looked wrong
- **`CallableEmitter::signature()` never uses its `$meta` parameter.** Type edges take their location from where the type is written; the new `testSignatureRecordsEachTypeWhereItIsWritten` pins that.
- **This engine always reports column 1.** Every emitter hard-codes it.
